topic: Overloading Universal References [Problem]: Type Disparity Filtering
explanation: Overloading a universal reference constructor, $C(T\&\&)$, necessitates precise type filtering to prevent it from acting as a hidden copy constructor when an lvalue of type $C$ is provided. Direct SFINAE checks comparing the deduced type $T$ against the class type $C$ fail because template argument deduction dictates that $T$ is deduced as an lvalue reference, $C\&$, for lvalue inputs. This type disparity causes $\text{std::is\_same}<T, C>$ to evaluate false, permitting unintended instantiation. To correctly filter out lvalues of the containing class, the programmer must normalize the deduced type using $\text{std::decay\_t}<T>$ before comparison. This normalization strips reference and cv-qualifiers, ensuring the check accurately identifies the base type $C$ and prevents the universal reference from capturing self-lvalues.
practical_example: A class template designed to handle arbitrary wrapped types fails its explicit move constructor logic because the universal reference constructor's simple type filter incorrectly allows the class's own type (wrapped in a reference) to instantiate the forwarding logic, causing unexpected runtime errors during resource transfer.
chapter: Item 26: Avoid overloading on universal references
